title: Milwaukee still absorbing budget at the account's lowest ROAS (2.57) — second week running
detail: PMax_Cube_Milwaukee is again the top spender at $1,143 (+$336 vs prior period) while returning ROAS 2.57 — the lowest of any real per-location campaign. Meanwhile the two best performers got cut: Whitefish Bay (ROAS 4.44) down $605 to $581, and Brookfield (ROAS 4.39) down $313 to $976. This is the same misallocation flagged last week and it widened. Unless the Milwaukee push is a deliberate MKE Public Market support play, moving ~$300-500/period from Milwaukee back into Brookfield/Whitefish Bay would buy conversions at roughly 1.7x the return. Recommend capping Milwaukee's budget and lifting the two high-ROAS campaigns.

title: PMax_Cube_Top Locations is now serving but at ROAS 1.20 — worst in the account
detail: Last week this campaign was ENABLED with zero delivery; it has since started serving ($146 spend, ROAS 1.20 vs account 3.57). That resolves the 'is it broken' question but confirms the cannibalization concern — it overlaps geographically with the per-location PMax campaigns and is converting at a third of their efficiency. Recommend pausing it (or narrowing its geo/asset targeting) so its budget flows back to the location campaigns rather than competing with them for the same impressions.

title: Sun Prairie ROAS fell 4.50 -> 3.74 (-0.75), the only campaign past the 0.5 drop threshold
detail: Even though spend was cut $365 to $581, PMax_Cube_Sun Prairie's return dropped three-quarters of a point — the sharpest ROAS decline in the account this period (it was a top-3 performer last period). No other campaign dropped more than 0.13. Worth a look in Google Ads for an asset-group or audience-signal change, or a seasonal softening in that market. Hold budget flat here until the return stabilizes rather than adding to it.

title: Account spend and conversion value both down ~25% for a second straight period
detail: Spend fell $9,569 -> $7,343 (-23%) and conversion value $35,177 -> $26,211 (-25%), while ROAS held roughly flat (3.68 -> 3.57) and CPA steady at $0.47. Efficiency is fine but volume keeps contracting two periods in a row — that is ~$9k/period in tracked conversion value now foregone. If this is intentional budget tightening, no action; if not, check for depleted shared budgets or pacing caps. The July 4 near-zero day (conv value $348) also drags the current window.

title: Meta: Catering video is the weakest campaign at $0.66/LPV vs $0.40 account average
detail: On flat total Meta spend ($671, +$89) and flat blended cost/LPV ($0.40 vs $0.39), the Catering Traffic 0326 video is a clear laggard — $160 spend for 244 landing-page views = $0.66/LPV, ~65% above average and the most expensive of the five. By contrast the new falafel launch 0706 ($0.35/LPV) and Branding traffic 0626 ($0.30/LPV) are the most efficient. Recommend shifting a portion of Catering's budget into those two, or refreshing the Catering creative before continuing to fund it at this rate.

title: Meta still has no purchase tracking — $671/period measured only on landing-page views
detail: All five Meta campaigns remain traffic-objective with no purchase/online-order events, so unlike Google (ROAS 3.57) the channel can only be judged on LPVs. This has carried unresolved for several weeks. Adding the Meta Pixel purchase/order-confirmation event (Toast confirmation page) would let Meta report conversion value and make the two channels directly comparable. The spend also still sits on a legacy personal-named ad account (act_35967094) worth migrating to the business account when convenient.
